bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet held net-cash: cash position (cash, fixed deposits and current investments) of Rs 11,208 mn in FY26, up from Rs 3,161 / 5,020 / 6,947 / 7,224 mn over FY22-FY25; nil borrowings at Mar-26.

- FY26 return ratios stated as ROCE 21.6% and ROE 16.2%, with Return on Invested Capital of 64.4%; the deck defines each ratio in a footnote.
- Management frames the philosophy as managing "the business with agility, discipline, and prudence" for "sustainable long-term growth and value creation", and asks that the business "be evaluated from an annualised and multi-year perspective".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership: approximately 73.5% share of India's SLCM market and second-largest concrete equipment manufacturer in India
- Distribution reach: 68 domestic dealers across 26 states, 132 customer touchpoints, 75 dedicated service professionals and 28 international distributors covering 56 countries
- Brand and pricing power: a 5% to 6% price premium supported by strong brand equity and superior resale value
- Highest SLCM resale value in the industry, 10-15% higher than the nearest competitor, reinforcing customer retention and enabling trade-in programmes
- In-house R&D: a 66-member design, engineering and development team; the only Indian company to develop a slip-form paver entirely in-house (2019) and the first to commercialize an indigenous 3D concrete printing machine (2023)
- Asset-light, lean manufacturing model using Andon, Just-in-Time, Kaizen, Poka-Yoke and online traceability, contributing to one of the lowest break-even levels among peers
- Localized supply chain: over 450 suppliers with nearly two-thirds located within 100-150 kilometres of the Bengaluru manufacturing facilities, localization above 90% and less than 10% of input materials imported
- Debt-free balance sheet providing strategic and financial flexibility
- Diversified customer base of approximately 23,000 end customers with minimal customer concentration risk
- Over 33,000 concrete equipment units sold in the last 10 years, creating a large installed fleet that drives spares and service annuity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Product and segment concentration in Self-Loading Concrete Mixers — The SLCM segment contributed 83.60% of revenue in 2025-26, so any loss of the approximately 73.5% SLCM market share, or a downturn specific to that product category, flows almost directly to the top line. Market share already dipped temporarily to roughly 70% in the first quarter before recovering.
- Competition and market share erosion — Aggressive pricing and unsustainable business practices by competitors may affect market position. The Company sustains a 5% to 6% price premium on brand equity, superior resale value and a 132-touchpoint after-sales network - a premium that is vulnerable if competitors discount hard.
- Dependence on government infrastructure spending and project execution — Public investment is the key demand driver. Slower project execution and only 55% central capex utilization by December 2025 created demand headwinds in 2025-26, and shifts in government expenditure priorities may affect the pace of infrastructure investment and equipment demand. The cautionary statement names a downtrend in government spend on agriculture and infrastructure as a key risk factor.
- Customer cash flow, payment delays and credit risk — Slower execution of infrastructure projects and delayed payments have strained contractor cash flows, leading to deferment of equipment purchases. Mitigated by an asset-light operating model, a debt-free balance sheet and strong liquidity, but demand timing remains outside the Company's control.
- Regulatory and emission-norm transition costs — The CEV-IV to CEV-V transition, effective January 1, 2025, raised blended direct material cost by over 400 basis points and caused temporary market disruption from competitor inventory liquidation, pressuring margins across the industry. Future emission or regulatory transitions carry the same cost and inventory-management exposure.
- Commodity and input-cost inflation, particularly steel — Steel is the primary raw material across the product portfolio; volatility in steel and fuel prices may pressure manufacturing costs and the operating economics of equipment for customers. Mitigation relies on calibrated price increases that a soft demand environment can block, as happened for most of 2025-26.
- Geopolitical, currency and export-market risk — Geopolitical developments and currency fluctuations in key international markets may affect export growth and sentiment. Exports contributed 5 to 6.4% of operating revenue across 56 countries; the Company states it does not assume currency or country risk and focuses on selected priority markets, but growth ambition in exports raises the exposure.
- Operational and environmental / weather risk — Unseasonal rainfall and adverse weather can affect construction activity, machine utilization and demand for both equipment and spare parts - the latter a direct hit to the annuity spares and service revenue stream, which already grew despite lower average machine running hours in 2025-26.
- Strategic expansion and inorganic growth risk — The Company holds a large cash and investment position explicitly retained to fund the right opportunity; inorganic growth initiatives may expose it to financial and reputational risks. Mitigated by clearly defined acquisition guardrails and evaluation on strategic fit, governance standards and long-term value creation.
- Manufacturing and supplier geographic concentration — All operational and upcoming facilities are in Karnataka around Bengaluru, and nearly two-thirds of the 454 suppliers sit within 100-150 kilometres of those plants. The proximity that delivers cost and responsiveness advantages also concentrates disruption risk in one region.
- Governance and internal-control lapses — The Company entered into a related party transaction with a relative of a Director amounting to Rs 40,00,000 without the prior approval of the Audit Committee, which the Committee took a serious view of and ratified as a one-time exception. The statutory auditor also reported that the audit trail feature was not enabled throughout the year in the dealer/customer management software, and not enabled for direct data changes under certain access rights in the financial accounting software. A compounding penalty order of Rs 2,20,250 was received during the year.
- Key management transition — Substantial board and KMP churn: the Chief Financial Officer resigned in September 2025 with an Interim CFO appointed in December 2025, and three directors - Mr. Raghavan Sadagopan, Mr. Jacob Jiten John (a Promoter Director) and Mr. Rajan Wadhera - resigned between March and June 2026, alongside a stated 'moment of transition' for the company.

business.body:
- [Demand environment] The deck attributes FY26 and Q1 FY27 softness to industry headwinds: "Government spending remained below budgeted allocation", "Pace of project execution remained slow" and "Cash disbursement to contractors was delayed", with management adding that Q2 is "expected to remain seasonally soft" and momentum should strengthen in H2.
- [Industry TAM] India's Mechanised Concrete Equipment Industry is projected to grow from Rs 61 bn in FY24 to Rs 178 bn in FY29E, a 24% CAGR; mechanised penetration is projected to reach ~41% of domestic concrete consumption and ~28% of concrete equipment sales volume by FY29.
- [Skilling / R&D] Ajax School of Concrete is a dedicated R&D and training facility running "Specialised training programs for youth on concrete equipment operation, maintenance and safety" and research into "cost-effective and efficient 3D concrete printing solutions" and "optimal concrete mixes tailored for high-performance extrusion and sustainable construction".
- [Customer base] Customers grew from 11,000 in FY22 to 23,000 in FY26 (deck labels "+20%" CAGR) across rental companies, individual contractors, small/mid-sized contracting firms, large construction companies and government construction agencies, with the deck asserting "No customer concentration risk".

business.body: Ajax Engineering designs, assembles and sells equipment across the 360-degree concreting value chain - production, transportation, placement, paving and printing - having pioneered the Self-Loading Concrete Mixer in India in 1992. outlook.body:
- S1 - Maintain leadership and grow market share in the SLCM portfolio through continuous product enhancement, the CEV-V transition and smaller variants such as UDAAN that expand the addressable market
- S2 - Strengthen capabilities and increase market share of the non-SLCM portfolio (batching plants, transit mixers, concrete pumps), supported by the fifth manufacturing facility and a dedicated direct B2B sales channel across key metropolitan markets
- S3 - Improve operational efficiencies via a technology-led manufacturing ecosystem, lean operations and a highly localized supplier base to optimise cost and preserve flexibility
- S4 - Increase presence in overseas markets through exports, using an international distributor network across 56 countries with a disciplined approach to country and currency risk
- S5 - Explore inorganic growth opportunities, using a debt-free balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation to pursue acquisitions and partnerships assessed on return, governance standards and cultural fit
- Deepen distribution across both the dealer network and the B2B channel, including approximately 15 additional dealerships

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Ajax is expanding from four operational assembly and manufacturing facilities in Karnataka to five. The upcoming fifth facility at Adinarayanahosahalli, Doddaballapur, is designed with fungible, multi-product assembly lines, a flexible manufacturing configuration and scalable production infrastructure, and is expected to commence operations in H1 2026-27, strengthening production agility and supporting future growth across domestic and international markets. The existing footprint comprises Bashettihalli (established 1992, 19,340 sq. mt., SLCMs, concrete pumps, boom pumps and slip-form pavers), Gowribidanur (established 2014, 78,920 sq. mt., batching plants and transit mixers) and Obadenahalli (established 2018, 39,660 sq. mt., SLCMs), the last ranking among the world's largest SLCM manufacturing plants by area and running at approximately 67% capacity utilization in 2025-26, leaving headroom before the new plant ramps. All three operational sites are ISO 9001:2015 certified. Capacity investment is complemented by distribution build-out - an expansion of the dealer network through approximately 15 additional dealerships on top of 68 dealers, 132 customer touchpoints and 28 international distributors - and by the first full year of a direct B2B sales channel in metro markets. Environmental capex includes solar power installations at the Obadenahalli facility that have enabled energy self-sufficiency. The Company remains debt-free with a cash and investment position it describes as retained to fund the right opportunity, and continues to evaluate inorganic growth opportunities and partnerships that complement its design, engineering and supply chain capabilities. No rupee capex quantum for these projects is stated in the narrative sections of the report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Medium- and long-term outlook for India's infrastructure sector remains firmly positive, supported by continued urbanization, infrastructure modernization and the steady mechanization of construction; management expects these structural drivers to sustain demand for concrete equipment over the coming years
- Near-term demand will remain sensitive to external factors including the pace of government capital expenditure and project execution
- The Union Budget 2026-27 raised central capital expenditure by about 11% to approximately Rs 12.2 lakh crore, reinforcing the long-term sector outlook; however only 55% central capex utilization by December 2025 created temporary demand headwinds in 2025-26
- Government infrastructure programmes are a direct demand channel - Bharatmala, Dedicated Freight Corridors, PMAY (Urban and Rural), PM GatiShakti, Sagarmala and PMGSY - alongside Viksit Bharat 2047 targets of a 2 lakh km national highway network, 220 operational airports/heliports and 35 Multimodal Logistics Parks
- The ongoing shift toward mechanized concreting, growing adoption of ready-mix and precast construction, and rising project complexity support gradual, steady adoption of concrete equipment
- India is the world's third-largest construction equipment market targeting the second spot by 2030; industry sold 1,36,995 units in 2025-26 and is expected to reach approximately 2,50,000 units by the end of the decade
- The global concrete machinery market is estimated at USD 20.80 Billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 28.11 Billion by 2033, a CAGR of 4.4%, with Asia-Pacific at 45.2% of the market and the Middle East the fastest-growing region
- Global construction demand growth is projected at 3.92% in 2027 with emerging markets - South Asia, Southeast Asia and MENA - outpacing advanced economies, offering a resilient demand base for exporters
- Exports are expected to remain a key pillar of long-term growth, reinforcing the Make in India proposition; traction is building in Russia, Gabon, Belarus and Saudi Arabia, with the first slip-form paver export to Saudi Arabia establishing a credible new export line
- Margin lever: product mix and selective price increases held SLCM revenue steady despite a roughly 4% volume decline, against an estimated 11% decline for the broader construction equipment industry
- Margin headwind: the CEV-IV to CEV-V transition raised blended direct material cost by over 400 basis points, and a soft demand environment constrained the ability to pass on price increases for most of the year
- Demand for higher-capacity batching plants of 45 cubic meters and above improved, and the first full year of the direct B2B channel deepened engagement with large EPC and infrastructure players in metro markets
- Spares and services is an annuity driver tied to an installed base that now exceeds 35,000 machines, growing about 9% despite lower average machine running hours
- Customer cash flow strain from slower project execution and delayed payments is deferring equipment purchases
- Commodity and input-cost inflation, particularly steel and fuel prices, plus geopolitical and currency volatility in key export markets, remain watch items
- The UDAAN 0.75 cubic meter SLCM opens previously underserved applications - small residential projects, brick-making and rural infrastructure - expanding the addressable market
- Superior resale value (10-15% higher than the nearest competitor) supports structured trade-in programmes and customer retention

deepdive.thesis: Despite FY26 industry-wide demand slowdown and margin pressure from CEV5 transition costs, Ajax regained market share to 73.5% through disciplined pricing (2% Q4 hike), operational efficiency, and superior product reliability, with Q4 EBITDA margin rebounding to 15.1% and cash reserves surging to INR1,121cr — positioning it to capture infrastructure revival in H2FY27 with focus on non-SLCM growth and potential M&A.

currentContext.expansion: Ajax is expanding from four operational assembly and manufacturing facilities in Karnataka to five. The upcoming fifth facility at Adinarayanahosahalli, Doddaballapur, is designed with fungible, multi-product assembly lines, a flexible manufacturing configuration and scalable production infrastructure, and is expected to commence operations in H1 2026-27, strengthening production agility and supporting future growth across domestic and international markets. The existing footprint comprises Bashettihalli (established 1992, 19,340 sq. mt., SLCMs, concrete pumps, boom pumps and slip-form pavers), Gowribidanur (established 2014, 78,920 sq. mt., batching plants and transit mixers) and Obadenahalli (established 2018, 39,660 sq. mt., SLCMs), the last ranking among the world's largest SLCM manufacturing plants by area and running at approximately 67% capacity utilization in 2025-26, leaving headroom before the new plant ramps. Capacity investment is complemented by distribution build-out - an expansion of the dealer network through approximately 15 additional dealerships on top of 68 dealers, 132 customer touchpoints and 28 international distributors - and by the first full year of a direct B2B sales channel in metro markets. Environmental capex includes solar power installations at the Obadenahalli facility that have enabled energy self-sufficiency. The Company remains debt-free with a cash and investment position it describes as retained to fund the right opportunity, and continues to evaluate inorganic growth opportunities and partnerships that complement its design, engineering and supply chain capabilities. No rupee capex quantum for these projects is stated in the narrative sections of the report.

- Near-term demand will remain sensitive to external factors including the pace of government capital expenditure and project execution
- The Union Budget 2026-27 raised central capital expenditure by about 11% to approximately Rs 12.2 lakh crore, reinforcing the long-term sector outlook; however only 55% central capex utilization by December 2025 created temporary demand headwinds in 2025-26
- Government infrastructure programmes are a direct demand channel - Bharatmala, Dedicated Freight Corridors, PMAY (Urban and Rural), PM GatiShakti, Sagarmala and PMGSY - alongside Viksit Bharat 2047 targets of a 2 lakh km national highway network, 220 operational airports/heliports and 35 Multimodal Logistics Parks
- The ongoing shift toward mechanized concreting, growing adoption of ready-mix and precast construction, and rising project complexity support gradual, steady adoption of concrete equipment
- India is the world's third-largest construction equipment market targeting the second spot by 2030; industry sold 1,36,995 units in 2025-26 and is expected to reach approximately 2,50,000 units by the end of the decade
- The global concrete machinery market is estimated at USD 20.80 Billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 28.11 Billion by 2033, a CAGR of 4.4%, with Asia-Pacific at 45.2% of the market and the Middle East the fastest-growing region
- Global construction demand growth is projected at 3.92% in 2027 with emerging markets - South Asia, Southeast Asia and MENA - outpacing advanced economies, offering a resilient demand base for exporters
- Exports are expected to remain a key pillar of long-term growth, reinforcing the Make in India proposition; traction is building in Russia, Gabon, Belarus and Saudi Arabia, with the first slip-form paver export to Saudi Arabia establishing a credible new export line
- Margin lever: product mix and selective price increases held SLCM revenue steady despite a roughly 4% volume decline, against an estimated 11% decline for the broader construction equipment industry
- Margin headwind: the CEV-IV to CEV-V transition raised blended direct material cost by over 400 basis points, and a soft demand environment constrained the ability to pass on price increases for most of the year
- Demand for higher-capacity batching plants of 45 cubic meters and above improved, and the first full year of the direct B2B channel deepened engagement with large EPC and infrastructure players in metro markets
- Spares and services is an annuity driver tied to an installed base that now exceeds 35,000 machines, growing about 9% despite lower average machine running hours
- Customer cash flow strain from slower project execution and delayed payments is deferring equipment purchases
- Commodity and input-cost inflation, particularly steel and fuel prices, plus geopolitical and currency volatility in key export markets, remain watch items
- The UDAAN 0.75 cubic meter SLCM opens previously underserved applications - small residential projects, brick-making and rural infrastructure - expanding the addressable market
- Superior resale value (10-15% higher than the nearest competitor) supports structured trade-in programmes and customer retention

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Ajax is expanding from four operational assembly and manufacturing facilities in Karnataka to five. The upcoming fifth facility at Adinarayanahosahalli, Doddaballapur, is designed with fungible, multi-product assembly lines, a flexible manufacturing configuration and scalable production infrastructure, and is expected to commence operations in H1 2026-27, strengthening production agility and supporting future growth across domestic and international markets. The existing footprint comprises Bashettihalli (established 1992, 19,340 sq. mt., SLCMs, concrete pumps, boom pumps and slip-form pavers), Gowribidanur (established 2014, 78,920 sq. mt., batching plants and transit mixers) and Obadenahalli (established 2018, 39,660 sq. mt., SLCMs), the last ranking among the world's largest SLCM manufacturing plants by area and running at approximately 67% capacity utilization in 2025-26, leaving headroom before the new plant ramps. All three operational sites are ISO 9001:2015 certified. Capacity investment is complemented by distribution build-out - an expansion of the dealer network through approximately 15 additional dealerships on top of 68 dealers, 132 customer touchpoints and 28 international distributors - and by the first full year of a direct B2B sales channel in metro markets. Environmental capex includes solar power installations at the Obadenahalli facility that have enabled energy self-sufficiency. The Company remains debt-free with a cash and investment position it describes as retained to fund the right opportunity, and continues to evaluate inorganic growth opportunities and partnerships that complement its design, engineering and supply chain capabilities. No rupee capex quantum for these projects is stated in the narrative sections of the report.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, disciplined, resilient; emphasizes brand moat, customer loyalty, operational efficiency; avoids overpromising on guidance; cautious on macro but optimistic on structural demand

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership: approximately 73.5% share of India's SLCM market and second-largest concrete equipment manufacturer in India
- Distribution reach: 68 domestic dealers across 26 states, 132 customer touchpoints, 75 dedicated service professionals and 28 international distributors covering 56 countries
- Brand and pricing power: a 5% to 6% price premium supported by strong brand equity and superior resale value
- Highest SLCM resale value in the industry, 10-15% higher than the nearest competitor, reinforcing customer retention and enabling trade-in programmes
- In-house R&D: a 66-member design, engineering and development team; the only Indian company to develop a slip-form paver entirely in-house (2019) and the first to commercialize an indigenous 3D concrete printing machine (2023)
- Asset-light, lean manufacturing model using Andon, Just-in-Time, Kaizen, Poka-Yoke and online traceability, contributing to one of the lowest break-even levels among peers
- Localized supply chain: over 450 suppliers with nearly two-thirds located within 100-150 kilometres of the Bengaluru manufacturing facilities, localization above 90% and less than 10% of input materials imported
- Debt-free balance sheet providing strategic and financial flexibility
- Diversified customer base of approximately 23,000 end customers with minimal customer concentration risk
- Over 33,000 concrete equipment units sold in the last 10 years, creating a large installed fleet that drives spares and service annuity

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: delayed govt capex execution; state payment delays (Maharashtra, UP); El Niño impact on construction; global fuel price volatility; competitor price undercutting; currency/geo risks in export markets

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Dealer inventory at 35-40 days; 2% price hike taken in Jan FY26 — only player to do so; CEV5 product was 'first-time right' due to prior CEV3-CEV4 transition learnings; Udaan volumes are embedded in SLCM segment

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- S1 - Maintain leadership and grow market share in the SLCM portfolio through continuous product enhancement, the CEV-V transition and smaller variants such as UDAAN that expand the addressable market
- S2 - Strengthen capabilities and increase market share of the non-SLCM portfolio (batching plants, transit mixers, concrete pumps), supported by the fifth manufacturing facility and a dedicated direct B2B sales channel across key metropolitan markets
- S3 - Improve operational efficiencies via a technology-led manufacturing ecosystem, lean operations and a highly localized supplier base to optimise …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demand environment] The deck attributes FY26 and Q1 FY27 softness to industry headwinds: "Government spending remained below budgeted allocation", "Pace of project execution remained slow" and "Cash disbursement to contractors was delayed", with management adding that Q2 is "expected to remain seasonally soft" and momentum should strengthen in H2.
- [Industry TAM] India's Mechanised Concrete Equipment Industry is projected to grow from Rs 61 bn in FY24 to Rs 178 bn in FY29E, a 24% CAGR; mechanised penetration is projected to reach ~41% of domestic concrete consumption and ~28% of concrete equipment sales volume by FY29.
- [Skilling / R&D] Ajax School of Concrete is a dedicated R&D and training facility running "Specialised training programs for youth on concrete equipment operation, maintenance and safety" and research into "cost-effective and efficient 3D concrete printing solutions" and "optimal concrete mixes tailored for high-performance extrusion and sustainable construction".
- [Customer base] Customers grew from 11,000 in FY22 to 23,000 in FY26 (deck labels "+20%" CAGR) across rental companies, individual contractors, small/mid-sized contracting firms, large construction companies and government construction agencies, with the deck asserting "No customer concentration risk".
